correctness.rationale: The joint generator closes exactly on 1, X^2, X^4, L, LX^2, L^2; stationary moments are 2D/k and 24D^2/[k^2(1+q^2)]. Solving ODEs proves all-time mean/variance and unique 1-5q^2 cancellation; a separate Ito energy identity yields the Gaussian martingale limit. Conditioning on exactly one reset and a stationary bilateral-exponential summand proves every positive exponential moment infinite. A standalone six-dimensional generator matrix gave 3889 checks across 648 parameter cases; finite checks are not proofs of infinite statements.

originality.rationale: The claimed novelty is the exact all-time variance and sharp unique contraction q=1/sqrt(5), together with Gaussian large-time fluctuations despite divergence of every positive exponential moment for the specified instantaneous quadratic jump-loss functional. Full original model and closest work sources provide underlying stationary moments or different thermodynamic protocols, not this conclusion. Actual research-record searches and accessible prior own claims revealed no same or stronger implication. Residual risk remains from general affine-jump additive-functional theory and unindexed priority results.
residual_risks: An unpublished or nonindexed affine-jump additive-functional result could imply the exact variance as a specialization.
The practical thermodynamic meaning of instantaneous loss depends on the physical reset mechanism; no equality to finite-duration return work is asserted.
Search of scholarly records and published literature cannot certify global novelty; no independent audit is claimed.

value.rationale: The motivating physics has a mean energetic rate exactly insensitive to resetting contraction, while its finite-window loss fluctuations show a sharp exactly linear point q=1/sqrt(5), two opposite memory-correction regimes, and extreme-tail non-Cramer behavior despite Gaussian averaging. This quantitatively identifies sensitivity hidden by the mean, a motivated resetting-thermodynamics sampling question, not a routine re-expression of stationary position moments.
